title: test(gantt): anchor both contractEnvelope-6839 refusal arms on completion, and diagnose the six siblings
body:
Part of #8665. That card asks for a component-level diagnosis of seven `contractEnvelope-6839` siblings and names two as vacuous in the refusal direction. One of the two is; the other is not, and the probe says why.

## What was measured, not read

⚠️ Every characterisation in #8665 is a reading of a wait EXPRESSION. Probed at the component, one of the two nominations does not hold.

### The family shares an idiom, and `plugin-gantt` was the one file missing it

Eight of the nine DOM files settle the fetch explicitly before they read:

```
await find.mock.results[0].value;   // find's OWN answer, settled
```

`plugin-gantt` had **zero** occurrences. That single omission is what made it the measurably vacuous one.

### `plugin-gantt/ObjectGantt` — REPAIRED (both sinks)

⭐ LEG 1, sink 2, with **no bug reintroduced at all** — the LIVE `data` envelope, rows answering immediately and the quick-filter domain one macrotask later:

| shape | what the arm read | what the same mount settled to |
|---|---|---|
| old | `offersP3=false offered=[p1]` | `offered=[p1,p2,p3]` |
| new | `offersP3=true offered=[p1,p2,p3]` | `offered=[p1,p2,p3]` |

The refusal assertion `expect(offersUnloadedProject(view)).toBe(false)` **passed against a component that resolved the whole domain**. It was measuring the polling tick, not the envelope. Same result at 50ms and at 300ms.

LEG 1, sink 1, uniform delay: the DOM at the old wait was the `Loading Gantt chart...` placeholder and the read threw `Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="gantt-view"]`. ⚠️ Reported honestly as a **spurious red, not a silent pass** — I could not construct a state where sink 1 passes vacuously, because `gantt-view` renders only below the `if (loading)` early return.

LEG 2 (new wait under the same forced ordering) and LEG 3 (ordinary ordering): every arm correct at 0ms / 50ms / 300ms, rows-late and domain-late alike.

**Anchors chosen from the component's own mechanism**

- sink 1 waits for `gantt-view`. `loading` is cleared in `reload`'s `finally`, in the same `isCurrent()`-guarded commit as `setData`, so its presence proves the row query settled AND committed.
- sink 2 anchors on a **control dimension**. `ObjectGantt` publishes no DOM marker for the domain fetch on the refusing branch — a refused domain leaves `lookupOptions[field]` empty, the resolver falls through to "distinct values present in the loaded data", and the dropdown looks exactly as it does before the fetch answers. So the fixture adds a second lookup (`owner`) resolved by the same effect: `setLookupOptions` is called once, after the loop over every dimension, and no loaded task carries an `owner`, so its option can only come from the domain fetch having been read and committed.

Both anchors are PRESENCE assertions, so neither arm can pass by timing out.

**Would an implementation strictly worse than the bug pass?** Ablating `extractRecords` to "return nothing, ever":

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| sink 2 refusal arm | PASSED | **FAILS** (`Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="quick-filter-option-owner-u1"]`) |

sink 1's refusal arm still reads 0 under that ablation; its positive arms refuse it. That is the whole family's documented design — all nine behave this way, the already-repaired `plugin-tree` included — so it is stated rather than claimed fixed.

### `plugin-dashboard/ObjectPivotTable` — NOT repaired, premise falsified

The card says the wait `queryByTestId('pivot')` cannot separate *"drawn empty"* from *"drawn before the data arrived"*. Measured, it can — and the anchor is a line the card's reading skipped, two lines above the wait it quotes.

With the `records` arm reintroduced ahead of `data` (the pre-fix bug), the refusal arm **reddens** at 0ms, 50ms and 300ms. It still reddens with `ObjectPivotTable`'s loading-skeleton early return also disabled. Removing only the settle line, it goes vacuous exactly as predicted:

| settle line | delay | arm reads | component drew | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| present | 300ms | 2 | 2 | FAILS — discriminates |
| removed | 50ms | 0 | **2** | PASSES — vacuous |

⇒ the file already carries its completion anchor. Left alone deliberately.

## The other five — diagnosed, not touched

All five carry the settle-line idiom, and in every one the waited-for node sits below a `loading` early return, so the wait is gated twice.

| file | component-side mechanism | does the wait fail to gate the read? | a repair would anchor on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin-calendar/ObjectCalendar` | `loading` starts `true`; `if (loading)` returns a placeholder, so the stubbed grid cannot mount early. Its comment calls the testid a mount signal — true and deliberate: it is envelope-INDEPENDENT, which is what lets one wait serve every arm. | No. Gated by `loading` and by the settle line. | Nothing needed. If hardened: assert the placeholder was observed, so the transition is two observations. |
| `plugin-charts/ObjectChart` | ⭐ The card flags the lazy boundary. `React.lazy` lives in `ChartRenderer.tsx` — **which this pin `vi.mock`s away**, so the pin never crosses it. The refusal arm asserts `'empty-state'`, a DIFFERENT node from the renderer, gated by `if (loading && finalData.length === 0)`. | No — and the kanban kinship does not transfer. Same shape of finding as tree-vs-kanban in PR #8664. | Nothing for the wait. ⚠️ Separate weakness, different class: site 2's refusal asserts `.not.toBe('Apollo')`, which `undefined` satisfies — the objectui#8688 shape. Filed separately. |
| `plugin-dashboard/ObjectDataTable` | Same two-branch shape PR #8664 replaced, but here both branches are presence-shaped and the refusal arm asserts `'empty-state'` — a distinct node, not a count of 0. `if (loading && finalData.length === 0)` gates both. | No. | Nothing needed. |
| `plugin-map/ObjectMap` | `loading` starts `true`; `setLoading(false)` commits with `setData`. Correct at 0/50/300ms with and without the settle line. | No — but ⚠️ it is the only absence-shaped wait of the five, and **at 0ms the `Loading map...` panel is never observed at all**, so the wait is satisfied with no transition having occurred. It holds only because those two setStates commit together, and nothing pins that. | Assert the panel was present first, or a positive post-settle node. The precondition, not the ordering. |
| `plugin-timeline/ObjectTimeline` | `if (loading && (!effectiveItems \|\| effectiveItems.length === 0))` gates the renderer. | No — but the wait says less than it looks: `getByTestId` throwing inside `waitFor` is what gates it; the `data-item-count` `.not.toBeNull()` half is inert, satisfied by `'0'`. | The count half is decoration. A repair would name the renderer's mount and drop the attribute check, or assert the drawn shape. |

⛔ No component was changed. Two component-layer findings are reported to the card, not fixed here.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-gantt/` — **64 files, 502 tests, all passed**.
- `tsc -p packages/plugin-gantt/tsconfig.test.json` with the dependency closure built (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-gantt^...' build`) — exit 0, **TS2307 count 0** so the precondition was met, and `--listFiles` confirms the changed file is in the program.
- `eslint .` in `@object-ui/plugin-gantt` — 92 files, **0 errors**, exit 0. Warnings 362 (package-wide, pre-existing). The changed file went 6 → 9 `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` warnings: three new helpers typed `view: any`, matching the convention every helper in that file already uses.
- `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:control-bytes`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` — all exit 0.
- Ablations mutated the READ SITE (`extractRecords`), never a pin, from a committed tree, with `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM, absolute paths, on-disk proof in both directions (anchor counts AND `git hash-object` vs the HEAD blob) plus a line-total gate, and restore proven by state (`git diff HEAD` empty).
- ⚠️ Two probe legs were VOID and are reported as void, not as readings: a first `plugin-map` probe omitted the pin's `react-map-gl/maplibre` mock and measured nothing, and a first pass leaked containers across runs. Both were rebuilt before any conclusion was drawn.

Changeset: empty frontmatter — test-only, releases nothing.
